commits.message:
[marina] Validate applets against runtime constraints (#8944)

`marina publish --dry-run` validated archive layout but did not import a
declared backend, and packaged HTML could retain inline JavaScript that
Marina's
`script-src 'self'` policy blocks. Running an applet backend from source
could
also create `server/__pycache__` files that the next package build
rejected.

Add `marina validate` to package the applet and import its backend in
the
current Marina Python environment with the isolated module layout used
after
upload. Its report lists completed checks and leaves factory execution,
migration execution, and browser behavior under `not_checked`;
package-only dry
runs also list backend imports there for Python applets. Package
validation
rejects executable inline `<script>` elements in uploaded HTML, and
local
package builds omit bytecode while retaining the existing allowlist of
`applet.toml`, `dist/`, and Python files under `server/`.

Only installed `lib/*` packages declared by
`infra/marina/pyproject.toml`
supply shared Marin helpers; imports from checked-in Marina apps are
unsupported. The docs use
`marin.evaluation.archive.sample_from_archive_row` as
the eval-reader example, add static HTML, Vue, and Python backend
starters, and
show how a second publish can update a running `--local` stack without
replacing
Postgres.

Fixes #8935
